correctness.rationale: Prefix extension exhausts all ternary square-free linear words because any newly created square is a suffix. Exact generation gives 168546 words at length 36 and 219516 at length 37. Direct cyclic testing gives 16416 and 18870 circular-square-free linear representatives. Two independent extremality procedures agree exactly on 540 length-36 representatives. Square-freeness forces primitivity, hence 36 rotations per circular class and exactly 15 classes. Exhaustive action of the six alphabet permutations and reversal yields orbit sizes 6, 6, and 3.

evidence: Theorem 1.3 gives the exact attainable length set and identifies 36 as the final sporadic length before 37 and the interval beginning at 38.
The proof says that for attainable lengths below 470 an extremal circular word was found by computer search, an existence statement rather than an exhaustive count.
No inspected later or broader source supplied the length-36 count or symmetry orbits.
broader_coverage.reasoning: An existence spectrum does not imply how many equality objects occur at an attainable length, and exponential-growth remarks likewise do not determine the exact finite boundary census.

value.rationale: Length 36 is not an arbitrary finite slice: it is the final sporadic attainable length in the exact published spectrum, immediately before the sole boundary failure at 37 and the eventual interval beginning at 38. A complete equality census there reveals three distinct symmetry types hidden by an existence-only theorem and gives a sharp reproducible description of the exceptional boundary.
